settings.title: Server address
settings.summary: The address and port Keystone listens on.
settings.description: The address and port Keystone listens on. The default is reachable from this machine only.

settings.title: Admin step-up length
settings.summary: How long the admin area stays open after the password is asked again.
settings.description: How long the admin area stays open on one session after an admin enters their password or uses a passkey again, never past the session's own end. After it, every admin route asks again (P15-01, decision 0643).

settings.title: HTTPS-only cookie
settings.summary: Marks the sign-in cookie for HTTPS only.
settings.description: Whether the session cookie is marked for HTTPS only. Turn it on once Keystone is reached over HTTPS. A request that arrives over HTTPS gets the mark whatever this says.

settings.title: Request size
settings.summary: The largest request the server reads.
settings.description: The most bytes the API reads from one request's body. A larger body is refused.

settings.title: Stream heartbeat
settings.summary: How often a quiet stream says it is still there.
settings.description: How often an open stream sends a line that means only that it is still there, so nothing between Keystone and the browser closes a quiet connection.

settings.title: List page size
settings.summary: The most rows a list returns in one call.
settings.description: The most rows a list in the API returns in one call. A client reads further pages to get the rest.

settings.title: Names on the sign-in screen
settings.summary: Shows the names of the people here before anyone signs in.
settings.description: Whether the API tells someone who has not signed in the names of the people on this install, so the sign-in screen can ask who is signing in. Off, a person must know their own id.

settings.title: Password hashing rounds
settings.summary: How hard a stored password is made to guess.
settings.description: How many rounds of PBKDF2-SHA-256 a password goes through before it is stored. More rounds make a stolen database slower to guess from. A stored password moves to the new count the next time its person signs in.

settings.title: Password length
settings.summary: The fewest characters a new password may have.
settings.description: The fewest characters a new password may have.

settings.title: Sign-in lifetime
settings.summary: How long a sign-in lasts before a person signs in again.
settings.description: How long a sign-in lasts before the person must sign in again.

settings.title: Wrong passwords allowed
settings.summary: How many wrong passwords in a row before a wait.
settings.description: How many wrong passwords in a row are taken before password sign-in makes the person wait.

settings.title: Wait after wrong passwords
settings.summary: How long sign-in is refused after too many wrong passwords.
settings.description: How long password sign-in is refused after too many wrong passwords in a row.

settings.title: Passkeys
settings.summary: Lets people add passkeys and sign in with them.
settings.description: Whether people may add passkeys and sign in with them. Off until the sign-in screen has proven them in a browser.

settings.title: Passkey host name
settings.summary: The host name passkeys are bound to.
settings.description: The host name passkeys are bound to, which must be the host people reach Keystone by. Changing it makes every stored passkey unusable.

settings.title: Passkey page address
settings.summary: The address a passkey must be used from.
settings.description: The address in the browser's bar when a passkey is used: scheme, host and port. A passkey answer from any other page is refused.

settings.title: Passkey prompt time
settings.summary: How long a person has to answer a passkey prompt.
settings.description: How long a person has to answer a passkey prompt before it must be asked again.

settings.title: Load the test person
settings.summary: Adds the invented test person when Keystone is rebuilt.
settings.description: Whether rebuild loads the test tenant into the data folder: an invented person whose password is published in the repo, with a few chats and the fake provider for a model. Switch it off on an install that people outside the home can reach.

settings.title: Backup passphrase rounds
settings.summary: How hard a backup's passphrase is made to guess.
settings.description: How many rounds of PBKDF2-SHA-256 turn a backup's passphrase into its key, from 100000 to 50000000. More rounds make a stolen backup slower to guess from. A backup records its own count, so a change applies to the next backup only.

settings.title: Backup passphrase length
settings.summary: The fewest characters a backup's passphrase may have.
settings.description: The fewest characters a backup's passphrase may have.

settings.title: Usage report period
settings.summary: The period the usage report opens on.
settings.description: The period the usage report shows when none is asked for: this month, last month, or the last 7 or 30 days, in calendar days in UTC as the monthly cap counts them.

settings.title: Usage report rows
settings.summary: How many lines each part of the usage report lists.
settings.description: How many lines each breakdown of the usage report shows, by model, by chat and by kind of work, costliest first, before the rest are added up in one more line. Below 1 is taken as 1.

settings.title: Longest usage report
settings.summary: The most days one usage report may cover.
settings.description: The most days one usage report may cover when it is asked for a range of days.

settings.title: Snapshot interval
settings.summary: How often each limit's level is recorded for its trend.
settings.description: How often the server records where each person's limits stand (the monthly cap, the memory reserve, the disk, their database, files and artifacts), so Operations can show each limit's trend. From 1m to 24h.

settings.title: Snapshots kept
settings.summary: How long a recorded level is kept.
settings.description: How long a snapshot of a limit is kept before it is removed. 840h is 35 days.

settings.title: Database room
settings.summary: The size a person's database is planned to grow to.
settings.description: The size, in megabytes, a person's database (keystone.db with its write-ahead log) is planned to grow to. Operations shows the database against it.

settings.title: Files room
settings.summary: The room set for one person's files.
settings.description: The room, in megabytes, set for one person's files folder: uploads and project files. Operations shows the folder against it.

settings.title: Artifacts room
settings.summary: The room set for one person's artifacts.
settings.description: The room, in megabytes, set for one person's artifacts folder. Operations shows the folder against it.

settings.title: Trend window
settings.summary: How far back Operations looks to tell a trend.
settings.description: How far back Operations looks to tell each limit's trend: its growth a day and when it would fill at that rate. 168h is a week; the monthly cap and the memory reserve look back no further than the start of the month.

settings.title: Shortest trend
settings.summary: How much history a limit needs before its trend is shown.
settings.description: How long a limit's snapshots must span before Operations tells its trend and when it would fill. Shorter, and a few minutes of a disk's churn read as a rate for the whole day. A run's budget is told from its own calls, whatever this says.

settings.title: Health window
settings.summary: The recent period model health is measured over.
settings.description: The recent window Operations reads each model's calls, errors, refusals and median time over, and the background tasks that failed.

settings.title: Tasks listed
settings.summary: How many recent tasks and runs Operations lists.
settings.description: How many of the newest background tasks and scheduled runs Operations lists, and how many of those that failed. From 1 to 100.

settings.title: Traces listed
settings.summary: How many recent traces Operations lists.
settings.description: How many of the newest traces Operations lists: each turn or run with its calls, tool steps, tokens, cost and outcome. From 1 to 100.

settings.title: Stuck after
settings.summary: How long a task runs before it is listed as stuck.
settings.description: A background task or scheduled run whose round has gone on longer than this, and is not paused or waiting for your approval, is listed as stuck on Operations.

settings.title: Model error warning
settings.summary: The share of failed calls at which a model is flagged.
settings.description: The share of a model's calls in the health window, in percent, that may fail before Operations shows the model as having errors.

settings.title: Disk warning
settings.summary: How full the disk gets before you are told.
settings.description: How full the volume that holds Keystone's data folder may get, in percent, before Operations and the home screen tell you.

settings.title: Database warning
settings.summary: How full your database gets before you are told.
settings.description: How much of its planned size your database may reach, in percent, before Operations and the home screen tell you.

settings.title: Files warning
settings.summary: How full your files folder gets before you are told.
settings.description: How much of its room your files folder may use, in percent, before Operations and the home screen tell you.

settings.title: Artifacts warning
settings.summary: How full your artifacts folder gets before you are told.
settings.description: How much of its room your artifacts folder may use, in percent, before Operations and the home screen tell you.

settings.title: Memory budget warning
settings.summary: How much of the memory budget is spent before you are told.
settings.description: How much of the memory pass's reserve may be spent in a month, in percent, before Operations and the home screen tell you. The monthly cap's own level is usage.cap_warn_percent.

settings.title: Run budget warning
settings.summary: How much of a run's budget is spent before you are told.
settings.description: How much of its own budget a background task or scheduled run under way may spend, in percent, before Operations and the home screen tell you.

settings.title: Data folder
settings.summary: The folder that holds everything Keystone stores.
settings.description: The folder that holds keystone.json and one folder for each tenant.

settings.title: Master key keeper
settings.summary: Where a new install keeps the key that protects secrets.
settings.description: Where a new install keeps the master key that protects every tenant's secrets. system is the operating system's key store: DPAPI on Windows, the login keychain on macOS, the Secret Service on Linux. file is a key file in the user's profile, for a machine with no key store, and is weaker. Once an install has stored a secret, keystone.json records the keeper and this setting is no longer read.
